questions.questionText: P sells a Laptop to Q at a loss of 25% and Q sells the laptop to R at a profit of 20%. If R purchased the laptop for ₹22,500, then what was the cost (in ₹) of the laptop for P?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: Praveen sells a study table to Zoya at a loss of 10%, and Zoya sells the study table to Aadarsh at a profit of 25%. If Aadarsh purchased the study table for ₹2,250, then what was the cost (in ₹) of the study table for Praveen?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: Akash sold a motorcycle to Navin at a profit of 10%. Navin sold it to Vinay at a profit of 20%. Vinay sold it to Vishal at a loss of 5%. If Vishal paid ₹62,700 for the motorcycle, then what was the cost of the motorcycle (in ₹) for Akash?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A sold an article to B at 25% profit and B further sold it to C by earning a certain profit. If the cost price of C is 30% more than the cost price of A, then find the profit percentage earned by B.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A tea seller used to make 50% of profit by selling tea at ₹9 per cup. When the cost of ingredients increased by 25%, he started selling tea at ₹10 per cup. What is his profit percentage now?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: Aditya buys 300 mangoes for ₹1,100. Some of these mangoes are rotten and are thrown away. He sells the remaining mangoes at ₹5 each and makes a profit of ₹150. Find the percentage of mangoes thrown away.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: The cost of manufacturing an item was ₹24,000, and 20% of it was spent on packaging and its shipment to a retailer. The manufacturer made a profit of 50%, while the retailer incurred a loss of 20% on selling it to a customer. At what price (in ₹) was the item sold by the retailer?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A company buys raw materials for ₹10,000 and manufactures a product that costs an additional ₹5,000 in labour and overhead. The product is sold to a distributor for ₹25,000, who marks it up by 20% and sells it to a retailer. The retailer then marks it up by another 25% and sells it to the end customer. What is the overall percentage profit made by the company, distributor, and retailer combined?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Sukhen purchased some perishable items for sale but 15% of those items could not be sold and went bad. however, Sukhen managed to sell the rest of the items at a price that helped him earn an overall profit of 19%. At what percentage above the cost price of each item did Sukhen sell each of the items that did NOT go bad?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: The cost prices of two articles A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5 While selling these articles, the shopkeeper gains 10% on article A and 20% on article B and the difference in their selling prices is ₹480 The difference in the cost price (in ₹) of articles B and A is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A costs thrice as much as B. A is sold at a loss of 10% and B is sold at $\frac{5}{4}$ of its own price. If the selling price of A is ₹5,800 more than the selling price of B, then the cost price of A is.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: The cost prices of two articles A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5. While selling these articles, the shopkeeper gains 10% on article A and 20% profit on article B, and the difference in their selling prices is ₹480. Find 30% of the total cost price (in ₹) of both the articles.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A wrist watch is sold for ₹1,200 at a profit percent equal to its cost price. Find the cost price of the wrist watch.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: By selling an article for ₹131.25, a trader gains as much percent as the number representing the cost price of the article. In order to earn 40% profit, at what price (in ₹) should he sell the article?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: Madhav purchased an item for ₹42,000 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With that amount, he purchased another item and sold it at a gain of 30%. What is the overall gain (in ₹)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: If a shopkeeper sells sugar at Rs.44.8 per kg, he is able to make a 12% profit. Due to water seepage, $\frac{1}{5}$ of the sugar is damaged. What should now be the selling price per kg of the rest of the sugar to have a 5% profit?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: An article passing through two hands is sold at a total profit of 40% of the original cost price. If the first dealer makes a profit of 30%, then the profit percentage made by the second dealer is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Raman fixes the sale price of his goods at 16% above the cost price. He sells his goods at 12% less than the fixed price. Find the profit percentage correct to two places of decimal.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Aarav owns a watch worth ₹10,000. He sells it to Bhavin at a profit of 15%. After some days, Bhavin sells it back to Aarav at 15% loss. Find the percentage profit or loss faced by Aarav.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A reduction of 7.5% in the cost price of a commodity enables a shopkeeper to purchase 15 kg more than what he previously purchased for a sum of ₹7,400. In order to make a profit of 32.5% on the pre-reduction cost price of the commodity, at what price (in ₹) per kg should the commodity be sold?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: The price of an item is increased by 15% and then the price is decreased by 12%. What is the effective percentage increase in the price of item?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A dealer buys an article listed at ₹250 and gets successive discounts of 12% and 16%. He spends 10% of the cost price on transportation. At what price should he sell the article to earn a profit of 25%? (Correct to two places of decimal)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: The first shirt is sold at twice the selling price of the second shirt. The first shirt is sold at 8% profit and the second shirt is sold at a 3% loss. What is the overall percentage profit on the shirts (Rounded off to two decimal place)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Sukhvir purchased some perishable items for sale but 30% of those items could not be sold and went bad. However, Sukhvir managed to sell the rest of the items at a price that helped him earn an overall profit of 19%. At what percentage above the cost price of each item purchased by Sukhvir did he sell each of the items that did not go bad?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Aditya sold article X at a profit of 23% and article Y at a loss of 13%. He earned a profit of ₹180 in the entire transaction. If article X costs ₹90 less than article Y, then what is the price of article Y (in ₹)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: A vendor marked the selling price of a table at ₹5,670 after adding 35% profit to its cost price. Since the sale was very low at this price level, he decided to sell the table with 12% profit. Find the new selling price (in ₹).
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Ankita sold three toys. The first toy was sold for ₹1,500 at a profit of 25%; the second toy was sold for ₹2,800 at a loss of 50% and the third toy was sold for ₹3,500 at a profit of 25%. Find her total profit or loss percentage.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: By selling a TV set for ₹16,800, a salesman gains a profit of 20%. If the production cost is increased by 20%, find the new selling price of the set so as to gain 20%.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: If a man purchases kismis at ₹320/kg and sells it at ₹6 per 25 grams. then his profit/loss percentage is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: The market price of cupboard is ₹15,750, which is 50% above its cost price. It is sold at a discount of 40%. What is the profit/loss percentage?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A person purchased ten boxes of grapes at a cost of ₹2,000 per box. Each box contained 20 kg of grapes. He sold each box at the rate of ₹2,500 per box. But on the whole 10 kg of grapes were damaged. Further he paid ₹1,000 as a transport charges. Find his gain or loss.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A fruit seller buys 480 bananas for ₹1,200. Some of these bananas are rotten and hence they are thrown away. He sells the remaining bananas at ₹3.5 each and makes a profit of ₹396. What is the percentage of bananas thrown away?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: The marked price of mustard oil is 25% more than its cost price. At what percentage less than the marked price should it be sold to have no profit and no loss?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: If the selling price of an article is doubled, then the profit becomes four times. What was the original profit percentage?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper purchases six small cold drink bottles for ₹100. For how much should he sell one such bottle to get a profit of 20%?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Ram bought a cell phone and paid 30% less than its original price. He sold it at 50% profit on the price he had paid. The percentage of profit earned by Ram on the original price was:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper is incurring a loss of cost price of 4 pens while selling 20 pens to Ajay. If the shopkeeper had purchased 20 pens at 10% less price and had sold 20 pens to Ajay at 25% more than the selling price, then how much percentage would he have gained (rounded off to 1 decimal place)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper bought articles A and B for a total ₹2,540. He sold A at a gain of 15% and sold B at a loss of 25%. The selling price of A was ₹109 more than that of B. His profit or loss percentage in the entire transaction was (rounded off to one decimal place):
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: The cost price of two articles A and B is the same. Article A is sold at a loss of 24% and article B is sold for ₹270 more than the selling price of A. If the net profit by selling both the articles is 12%, then what is the selling price (in ₹) of article B?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: $\frac{2}{5}$ of marked price is equal to $\frac{5}{8}$ of selling price. What is the discount percent?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: The cost price of two dozen bananas is ₹30. After selling 15 bananas at ₹12 per dozen, the shopkeeper sells the remaining bananas at ₹5 per dozen. What is the percentage of loss?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: Ritika purchased x kg wheat at ₹30/kg and sold 8 kg of this at ₹x per kg and remaining at ₹45/kg. Overall profit percent earned is 10%, then what quantity of wheat Ritika sold at ₹45/kg ?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A man buys a machine for ₹5,000. After one year, he sells it for ₹6000. After two years, again he buys the same machine at ₹8,000 and sells it for ₹10,000. Find his overall profit percentage for both the transactions.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Products pass successively through the hands of three traders and each of them sells his goods at a profit of 30% of his cost price. If the last trader sold the products for ₹300, then how much did the first trader pay for them?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: The price of some wooden furniture increases by 65% when it passes through three hands. If the first and second sellers made a profit of 20% and 25%, respectively, then find the profit percentage of the third seller.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: A Microwave oven is sold in Hyderabad for ₹M. A retailer, Elahi from Hyderabad went to Madras and bought it for 25% less (when compared to the price in Hyderabad). He spends ₹1,000 on transport to bring it from Madras to Hyderabad. He sold it in Hyderabad for ₹M making a profit of 10%. Find the value of M (in ₹).
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: What will be the actual profit percentage (rounded off to nearest integer) after selling an article at a certain price, while there occurs a loss of 45% on selling the article at $\frac{3}{8}$ of the selling price?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper increases the selling price of an article by 15%. After increasing the selling price, he noticed that the profit percentage changed from 5% to 15%. The percentage increase in the cost price is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: P buys an article for ₹280 and sells it to Q at a profit of 25%. Q sells it to R at some profit R sells it to S for ₹560 marking a profit of 40%. What percentage profit (rounded off to the nearest integer) did Q make?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Harsh purchased a scooter for ₹48,000. He sold it at a loss of 15%. With that money he purchased another scooter and sold it at a profit of 22.5%. What is his overall loss/profit percentage?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper bought 20 kg of sugar at ₹45 per Kg, 25 Kg of sugar at ₹50 per kg and 35 kg of sugar at ₹40 per kg. He spent a sum of ₹450 on transportation and other expenses. He mixed all the three types of sugar and sold all the stock at ₹52.50 per kg. His profit percent in the entire transaction is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: The cost price of articles X and Y is the same. Article X is sold at 20% profit and article Y is sold for ₹126 less than the selling price of X. If the net profit by selling both the articles is 14%, then what is the cost price (in ₹) of each article?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at $33\frac{1}{3}\%$ of this price, there is a loss of $33\frac{1}{3}\%$. What is the percent profit when it is sold at 60% of the original selling price?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A man sells his goods at a certain price, 20% of which is his profit. If the price at which he buys the goods increases by 10% and he sells then at an 8% higher price, then what will be his profit percent (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: The marked price of an article is ₹315. It is sold for ₹288. If there is a loss of 4%, then by what percent above the cost is the article marked?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).
